title: Loyalty Like the Morning Mist
overview: The chapter sets a hopeful call to return to the LORD beside God's lament that his people's loyalty fades like dew, then lists the violence and unfaithfulness filling the land.

parts.label: A call to return (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The people urge each other back to the LORD, trusting that the God who struck them will heal them soon ("two days" and "the third day" mean a short time), and come as surely as dawn and the rains that made crops grow. Christians later read the third day as pointing to Jesus rising from the dead.

parts.label: Loyalty that evaporates (vv. 4-5)
parts.note: God speaks to both kingdoms, Ephraim (the north) and Judah (the south), saying their devotion burns off like morning mist or dew. That is why he sent prophets whose words announced judgment as plainly as daylight.

parts.label: Loyal love over offerings (v. 6)
parts.note: The key word means steady, faithful love, and God says he wants that, along with truly knowing him, more than animal offerings. It is a ranking, not a ban: rituals mean little without faithfulness to God and to other people.

parts.label: A broken covenant (v. 7)
parts.note: The covenant was the binding agreement between God and Israel, and here the people break it. The comparison with Adam may mean the first man, a town called Adam by the Jordan River, or simply ordinary people, and scholars are unsure.

parts.label: Blood on the roads (vv. 8-10)
parts.note: Gilead, east of the Jordan, is called stained with blood, which may refer to men of Gilead helping assassinate King Pekahiah (2 Kings 15), and priests are pictured ambushing travelers on the road to Shechem like robbers. The prophet describes Israel's turning to other gods as sexual unfaithfulness, a picture he uses throughout the book.

parts.label: Judah's harvest too (v. 11)
parts.note: Judah will also reap what it has sown, a harvest of judgment. The line about God restoring his people is unclear, and some translations make it the start of the next chapter.

disagreement: Readers differ on whether the people's words in verses 1 to 3 are a real turning back that God welcomes or a quick, shallow repentance that the following verses expose.
think: In your own experience, what separates a change of heart that lasts from one that fades like morning mist?
